Angrist & Evans (1998) — Main Analysis

Reproduction tables, DML estimates, learner comparisons, and weight diagnostics

Alexander Unger

03 August 2026

Setup

Packages & Functions

Data & Design

Setting. Angrist and Evans (1998) childbearing application. The instrument is samesex; the treatment is morekids. The fixed diagnostic samples contain 3,000 observations for the primary labor outcome and 3,000 observations for the primary log-income outcome. They are created in ae98_make_balanced_subsample_submission.Rmd.

Common covariate design. Every estimator uses agem, agefstm, sexk, blackm, hispm, and othracem. The second-child sex indicator, sex2nd, is not included because, together with first-child sex, it deterministically reveals the instrument and creates exact collinearity within the instrument-specific nuisance regressions. The common six-variable design also makes the kappa, linear, forest, Ranger, and XGBoost comparisons use the same information set. Angrist and Evans report that removing the individual child-sex controls changes their estimates by no more than about two percent. See Angrist and Evans (1998).

Child-application analysis dimensions
Outcome N Pr(Z=1) Pr(D=1) Covariates
Work Status 3000 0.505 0.402 6
Maternal Log Income 3000 0.503 0.348 6

1. Reproduction — SUW Table 4 (split by outcome family)

The two tables reproduce the recoding structure of SUW Table 4 on the fixed diagnostic subsamples. They are not intended to reproduce the published full-sample point estimates.

2. Double ML — PLR-IV & Wald-AIPW (honest forest, tuned vs. untuned)

Each outcome-specific sample is fitted with untuned (tune.parameters = "none") and tuned ("all") honest forests. All four fits use five cross-fitting folds and seed 42.

3. Learner Comparison — PLR-IV and Wald-AIPW

The comparison uses the same learner families as Vietnam and Card. Every learner is fitted on the common six-covariate design introduced above, so differences are not confounded by learner-specific covariate sets.

4. Weight Diagnostics

The same candidate registry is used for the summary statistics, ESS and sign-cancellation results, and Love plots. Algebraic kappa weights and DML vectors that reproduce their fitted estimates are eligible. The honest-forest entries use the tuned fits; untuned fits remain in the tuning comparison.

Outcome-Weight Summary Statistics

The tables report statistics for the overall vector and its treated and sign-oriented control components. Neg. share is the fraction of observations with a negative oriented weight and differs from the absolute-mass sign-cancellation measure reported below. Only eligible representations are included.

ESS and Sign-Cancellation Extension

Modified ESS is reported separately for treated and control observations and relative to the observed size of each treatment arm. Opposite-sign mass is the percentage of absolute weight mass with the opposite orientation within the respective arm. It measures sign cancellation rather than the number of negative observations.

5. Love Plots

Panels report absolute mean differences. Continuous covariates are standardized; binary covariates remain on the raw 0/1 scale. Only candidates that pass the representation gate are plotted.
